title: Nyamwezi Groundnut Soup
community: Nyamwezi people of Tabora — the central plateau peanut soup
author: Mama Salima
desc: Nyamwezi Groundnut Soup — freshly roasted groundnuts ground and simmered with onion, tomato, and leafy greens into a thick, nourishing soup. The protein-rich staple of Tanzania's central plateau — sustaining traders and farmers alike for centuries.
longDesc: Groundnut soup is the Nyamwezi's most important source of plant protein — the freshly roasted and ground groundnuts produce a soup of extraordinary richness and body that sustained the great caravan traders on their journeys.
ingredients: 1 cup raw groundnuts — roasted and ground
steps: Roast groundnuts. Cool. Grind to a coarse paste.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden. Add tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes.
Mix ground groundnuts with 1 cup warm water.
Add to the tomato base. Add remaining water.
Add greens. Cook 3 more minutes until wilted.
chefTips: Fresh-roasted groundnuts are essential — commercial peanut butter lacks the roasted complexity.
The soup should be thick — not pourable.
cookingScience: See TZA049 for groundnut sauce science.
sustainabilityTips: Groundnuts are nitrogen-fixing — they improve the soil of the Nyamwezi plateau.
culturalNote: Nyamwezi groundnut soup is the food of the long road — nourishing enough to sustain traders walking hundreds of kilometres, made from a single drought-resistant crop that the central plateau provides in abundance.
